text:
tara: heads up — starter sample broken in edge: generics and overloads show as `any` for ESM consumers. CJS ok.

ben: can you paste a tiny repro?

tara: super tiny:
```ts
export function mapVal(x: string): string;
export function mapVal<T>(x: T): T;
export function mapVal(x: any) { return x }
```
Importing from dist/esm in a Next/nodenext app shows mapVal as (x: any) => any. No tsc errors.

yuki: classic: resolver looks for index.mjs.d.ts for the ESM export and falls back to any when missing. package.json exports + types mismatch.

oscar: also implementation using `any` can cause emit widenings. change impl to `function mapVal<T>(x: T): T { return x as T }` and regenerate d.ts to preserve generic.

tara: tried changing impl to generic -> d.ts better, but publishing pipeline still misses for some consumers.

yuki: recommended quick fixes: 1) add dist/types/index.d.ts and set "types" to it; 2) copy that d.ts to dist/esm/index.mjs.d.ts in postbuild; 3) add a tsd test importing dist/esm in CI.

ben: add short README note about nodenext vs bundler lookup. helps contributors.
\ci-bot: created issue #523 "starter: ESM consumers see collapsed overloads" and branch starter/fix-523.

tara: i'll open a small PR with postbuild copy + tsd job. assigning to eng-devex. Thanks!
